====Dealings with Axis====
=====Meeting with Luthen Rael=====
{{Quote|Kreegyr's a ''separatist''. Maya-Pei's a ''neo-republican''. The Ghorman front, the Partisan alliance, sectorists, human cultists, galaxy partitionists…they're ''lost!'' ''All'' of them! ''Lost!'' Lost. What are ''you'', Luthen? I've never really known.|Saw Gerrera, to Luthen Rael|<ref name="Narkina 5">{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}}</ref>}}
After the raid on the Imperial garrison on Aldhani<ref name="Aldhani">{{Andor|Aldhani (episode)}}</ref> in [[5 BBY]],<ref name="LargeDateNote" /> [[Luthen Rael]] traveled to Gerrera's base on [[Segra Milo]] and met with him. Getting down to business, Rael offered the freedom fighter the opportunity to trade several pieces of stolen Imperial technology, including a full set of Imperial drive adapters and three sealed [[Steergard]] targeting deflectors. After Rael confirmed that he had the items with him, Gerrera asked for him to set his price.<ref name="Narkina 5" />

[[File:Saw_Gerrera_Andor.png|left|thumb|267x267px|Saw Gerrera grew increasingly extremist as the Imperial era continued on.]]
To Gerrera's surprise, Rael asked that he meet [[Anto Kreegyr]], a contact who has been probing the [[Spellhaus Imperial power station|Imperial power station]] at [[Spellhaus]]. Rael continued by saying that Kreegyr has found some weaknesses in the defense, but that he had an angle. Since Kreegyr was a Separatist, Gerrera dismissed Rael's offer, but Rael insisted that Gerrera hear Kreegyr out. As Gerrera was unwilling to work with Kreegyr, Rael stated that technology would come on the condition that he work with Kreegyr, warning him that he would go to someone else if he did not comply.<ref name="Narkina 5" />

Gerrera insisted on working alone, but Rael asserted that that would have to change, telling Gerrera that they needed to work together to bring down the Empire. Gerrera persisted by saying that he was not a mercenary, but Rael asked him to imagine Spellhaus in flames. After listing a number of fallen rebel alliances, Gerrera asked what Rael was trying to accomplish. Rael responded by saying that he was a coward and was terrified that the Empire's power would grow beyond their means to stop it. He carried on by saying that they needed to put aside their differences, but Gerrera countered by claiming that he was the only one with clarity of purpose. Laughing, Rael stated that anarchy was a seductive concept for a man hiding in cold caves and begging for spare parts. Despite this, Gerrera refused to buy parts from Rael, telling him to find someone else to help Kreegyr.<ref name="Narkina 5" />

=====Second meeting with Rael=====
{{Quote|Thirty men.''"<br />"''Plus Kreegyr.''"<br />"''For the greater good.''"<br />"''Call it what you will.''"<br />"''Let's call it…war.|Saw Gerrera and Luthen Rael|<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix">{{Andor|Daughter of Ferrix}}</ref>}}
A little more than a month later, Gerrera had reconsidered his position and met with Rael a second time to join Kreegyr's attack on the Spellhaus power station. He told Rael that he would provide air power, but that aside from being told when it was needed he would be taking no tactical orders from Kreegyr and that his terms were non-negotiable. With the attack just a day away, Rael said he was too late. Since Gerrera would not back down so easily, Rael reluctantly explained that the ISB had learned of the imminent attack and would be waiting for the rebels on arrival at Spellhaus. Gerrera asked how Rael knew he would not warn Kreegyr, to which Rael replied that Gerrera was completely unpredictable. He continued by stating the decision to warn Kreegyr was now Gerrera's, but to consider the repercussions of both outcomes.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix" />

Deducing that Rael must have an informant in the ISB, Gerrera began looking around his HQ, wondering if a spy was among his own ranks. Rael said that Gerrera was avoiding the matter at hand, but Gerrera demanded to know who the spy was. Rael claimed Benthic was his man who told him everything, to which Benthic stepped forward in protest. Rael swiftly took Benthic's blaster from his holster and pointed it at Gerrera to get him to listen. Rael elaborated on how the ISB would become arrogant after Kreegyr's downfall, giving them a "clear field to play." He commented the alternative would lead to doubt and distrust in the ISB just as Gerrera is exhibiting now. Confirming a final time that thirty-one men would be sacrificed for this, Gerrera decided against warning Kreegyr for the sake of the war.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix" />

====The perfect night====
=====Rhydonium reverie=====
{{Quote|Have you ever seen a man die from rhydonium? Maybe you're like me, maybe you, you love… ''[sniffs]'' the smell of it. And maybe you breathe just a little too deeply. Burned from the inside. You watch your skin blister as it melts away. Or, you die loud. Cut a line? Drop a wrench? Let it spill? Don't even need a spark, do you, boy? Do you? Boom! Burn from the outside.|Saw Gerrera, to Wilmon Paak|<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />}}
By [[3 BBY]], Gerrera's Partisans established a base of operations on D'Qar. That year, Rael put [[Wilmon Paak]], an engineer belonging to Rael's Axis network, at Gerrera's disposal to manufacture a rhydonium mechanism. Paak presented the device to Gerrera who, admiring its loveliness, admitted it was a dream of his. Gerrera asked if it was "healthy" and had a full kit, which Paak confirmed, indicating its six gauges and eight variations.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />

Becoming excited, Gerrera lauded the technology to his guerrillas as a galaxy of opportunities; rhydonium on demand—what they wanted, when they wanted it. Gerrera asked Paak if the machine had been tested, to which he plainly stated that it worked. Demeanor shifting, Gerrera asked Paak who had taught him, leading Paak to question the inquiry in turn. Acknowledging rhydonium's high volatility and that few survived working with it, Gerrera reiterated his question. Paak replied that he was there to teach the variations and could not elaborate further.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />

Gerrera commended Paak's bravery, causing an eruption of laughter from the assembled Partisans, before asking if Paak had ever seen anyone die from rhydonium. Engaging in speculation, Gerrera wondered aloud if Paak, like himself, loved the smell of rhydonium; if inhaled too strongly, it would cause Paak's skin to blister as he combusted from the inside out. If Paak spilled it, cut a line, or dropped a wrench, Paak would ignite without a spark; immediate, explosive immolation.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />

Asking Paak's name, Gerrera dubbed him "the Boy," inquiring if he had any actual experience. Paak admitted that he'd configured the device twice, though never alone. Observing that Paak was still alive, Gerrera summoned Pluti and instructed Paak to teach him the variations, starting with Paak's favorite. Paak alluded that it would be helpful to know what station the Partisans intended to hit, but Gerrera refused to disclose the information. Stressing that he needed to leave the next day, Paak was refuted by Gerrera, who altered the deal, promising to tell Rael that Paak was being cared for. Gerrera ordered that accommodations be made for Paak, who would stay as long as Gerrera had need of him.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />

=====High on his own supply=====
{{Quote|Where are you, boy? You're here! You're not with Luthen. You're here! You're right here, and you're ready to fight!|Saw Gerrera, to Wilmon Paak|<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" />}}
Studying under Paak, Pluti approached Gerrera with an understanding of the variations, though he desired more practice. Gerrera asked if they could lose Paak, who knew too much, confirming if Pluti was ready. Pluti defended Paak as a great engineer and asked what they would tell whoever sent him, but Gerrera dismissed Pluti, preferring to write Paak off as an accident. When Pluti expressed disappointment that Paak would not join them, Gerrera claimed he lacked confidence. Pluti, overwhelmed, pressed Gerrera for the information to focus on a single variations. Gerrera revealed that the attack would target the Station Four junction of Neen Valley's Markez Moon pipeline, occurring the next night. Specifying that Tubes had the pipe numbers, Gerrera opted to keep Paak around for a while longer.<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" />

Later, Gerrera and Tubes approached Paak and Pluti. Gerrera asked Paak if Pluti could perform the operation independently, which Paak believed to be the case. Questioning his uncertainty, Gerrera raised a blaster to Paak's head, causing Paak to plead for his life. Gerrera instead executed Pluti, revealing him to be a traitor transmitting to the Empire. Having fed Pluti false information, Gerrera reassured the Partisans that they would not be caught in the ambush waiting for them on the Markez Moon, peacefully drinking rhydo parsecs away. Gerrera ordered the guerrillas to move quickly and burn what they did not take, as the Partisans would not be back to D'Qar.<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" />

Once the Partisans arrived at their actual target, Paak began calibrating the mechanism on a pipeline. As he waited, Gerrera began to tell a story from his younger days, reminiscing on his internment to a labour camp in the Onderonian jungle and the horrific conditions he faced, one of three hundred prisoners working in weather so hot they were forced to work naked. One day, everyone at the camp started to itch simultaneously, caused by a spillage of rhydonium that could be felt before being smelt. While everyone fled, Gerrera was the only one to stay, because the rhydo was "new" for him. Paak then succeeded in arming the device, which caused rhydonium steam to begin spilling from a valve in front of them.<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" />

Gerrera approached the steam with glee and muttered about his love for it, causing Paak to react with alarm and confusion as he began huffing the rhydonium with no side effects. Gerrera could do so because he understood the rhydo, loving it like a sister and calling the burn a joy. He suspected Paak thought him crazy, but instead admitted that he was; revolution wasn't for the sane, but the broken and hunted like them still stand, despite knowing they won't live to see the Republic reborn. He questioned where Paak was at that moment, then began to howl that he was right there with Gerrera and ready to fight. Inspired by Gerrera's words, Paak removed his protective mask and began painfully breathing in the rhydo, fueled by Gerrera's wild inspirations urging him to let it in. As Paak screamed in agony from the rhydo's burn, Gerrera cheered for him to let his newfound freedom run wild.<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" />

====Assassination of Moff Panaka====
{{Quote|The bombing was the work of a group that calls themselves the partisans, ''[sic]'' led by a man named Saw Gerrera. He's a brave man, an intelligent fighter…but his methods are becoming more violent, more extreme.|Breha Organa|<ref name="Leia">''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]''</ref>}}
[[File:SawGerrera-SWR.png|thumb|right|200px|Gerrera arranged for the assassination of Moff Panaka.]]
In 3 BBY,<ref name="Timelines" /> Gerrera, shaven his head bald again, arranged<ref name="TSWB">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> for a bomb to detonate at the [[Quarsh Panaka's chalet|residence]] of [[Moff]] [[Quarsh Panaka]]. The bomb achieved its objective of [[Strike on Onoam|killing]] the Moff who was supposedly one of the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor's]] most loyal servants. The timing of the bomb narrowly missed killing [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan]] and [[Naboo]]'s [[queen]] [[Dalné]], who had only just bid farewell to the Moff in his chalet moments before the explosion after discussing improving the working conditions of the [[miner]]s on [[Onoam]]. Although no real proof was ever given that Saw ordered the Moff's death, Leia's mother [[Breha Organa]]<ref name="Leia" /> correctly<ref name="TSWB" /> surmised that as leader of the Partisans, he must have been involved in some way and told Leia that she and her husband would be telling Saw how close he had come to murdering their daughter.<ref name="Leia" />

The assassination of Panaka greatly upset the rest of the rebels, who became increasingly frustrated at trying to keep the Partisans in line, as Panaka was the highest ranking member of the Emperor's inner circle that they had any hope of contacting some day and possibly even working with. With Saw's actions this was no longer a possibility. Princess Leia also didn't approve of Panaka's assassination as she viewed him as a good man though she initially allowed the Partisan she saw on Onoam to escape Imperial arrest as she feared that her parents may have been involved in the assassination, an accusation that greatly angered and offended Bail Organa.<ref name="Leia" />

Unbeknownst to Gerrera, his actions had indirectly saved Leia and her adoptive family as during Panaka's meeting with her and Danlé, Leia was wearing the [[jubilation dress]] that was once worn by her biological mother [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] which caused Panaka a great shock, and he managed to deduce Leia's heritage, unknown to even the princess at the time, and had planned on telling Palpatine however his death prevented this.<ref name="Leia" />

===Galactic Civil War===
====Mission to Geonosis====
{{Quote|The Empire is hiding something. Something important.|Saw Gerrera, to the Spectres|<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />}}
In [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Saw led a [[Mission to investigate Geonosis|mission to investigate]] the apparent [[Sterilization of Geonosis|disappearance]] of the [[Geonosian]] species of the planet [[Geonosis]].<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> His Partisan group had become one of the many cells that would form the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. Saw undertook the Geonosian mission on behalf of [[Alliance High Command|Rebel Command]] and Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]], an ally of the growing rebellion in the [[Imperial Senate]]. His team lost contact with Rebel Command after picking up an energy reading, which turned out to be an operational deflector shield generator.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

While exploring an underground labyrinth, Saw and his team were ambushed by [[Klik-Klak]],<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> the sole Geonosian to have survived the Sterilization of Geonosis.<ref name="Klik-Klak">{{Databank|klik-klak|Klik-Klak}}</ref> Klik-Klak's battle droids killed Saw's team but Saw managed to survive long enough for members of the [[Spectres]] rebel cell and Rex to rescue him. Saw saved the Spectres and Rex from a group of B1 battle droids and a droideka. Believing that the "bug" Klik-Klak was key to finding out why the Empire had exterminated the population of Geonosis, Saw convinced Rex and the Spectres to help him capture Klik-Klak.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

[[File:Saw_gerrera_on_Star_Wars_Rebels.png|thumb|left|250px|Saw Gerrera on Geonosis in 2 BBY.]]
While exploring the central air shaft, Saw and his team discovered Klik-Klak hiding on the other side. While the Spectres [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[C1-10P|Chopper]] pursued the Geonosian, Saw waited with Kanan and Rex when the Spectres' leader [[Hera Syndulla]] contacted Kanan. When Hera told them to leave, Saw convinced the Spectres to delay their stay so that they could complete his original mission to investigate the disappearance of the Geonosian species. Using [[the Force]], Kanan used a stone bridge to ferry Saw and Rex safely across to the other side of the air shaft.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

Once they had crossed, Saw and his rebel companions managed to corner Klik-Klak. Saw also shot out Klik Klak's remote controller with his blaster; deactivating several droidekas which were attacking the Spectres [[Sabine Wren]] and [[Garazeb Orrelios]] above. Saw then interrogated Klik-Klak and demanded to know what the Empire was building on Geonosis. Unable to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard]], Klik-Klak drew in the sand repeatedly. Ezra managed to befriend Klik-Klak. After Chopper picked up an energy reading, Saw forced Klik-Klak to lead them to the source.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

Saw and his companions soon discovered the energy reading came from [[Klik-Klak's nest]], which served as his workshop and contained a [[transmitter]]. Still bitter about the loss of his sister Steela at the hands of the Separatists, Saw aggressively questioned Klik-Klak and rummaged through his place. Saw's aggressive methods yielded no results while Ezra's gentler methods convinced Klik-Klak to reveal that he was the custodian of the last known Geonosian queen egg. Saw wanted to interrogate Klik-Klak off-world but Ezra objected on the grounds that Klik-Klak and the egg were among the last of their species and belonged on Geonosis. In the end, Kanan brokered a compromise whereby the rebels could question Klik-Klak at Chopper Base and then return him to Geonosis.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

Saw, his rebel allies and their prisoner Klik-Klak rendezvoused with the Spectres' ship ''[[Ghost]]'' in the central air shaft. Once aboard, Saw exchanged pleasantries with Hera and the rest of her crew. While Kanan and Hera were preoccupied, Saw reneged on his earlier agreement and tried to take Klik-Klak off-world on the shuttle ''[[Phantom II]]''. To force Klik-Klak's cooperation, Saw shocked him with an electro-shock device. This sparked an argument with the Spectres and Rex, who all objected to Saw's harsh methods. After fighting off Ezra and Rex, Saw threatened to destroy the Geonosian queen egg. In response, Ezra and Rex urged him not to become like the Empire he was fighting against.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

Saw's argument with the Spectres was interrupted by the arrival of [[Captain]] [[Brunson]]'s [[Brunson's Arquitens-class command cruiser|''Arquitens''-class command cruiser]], which blocked the air shaft and deployed a squad of [[Jumptrooper]]s to board the ''Ghost''. Saw joined the rebels in repelling the Imperial boarders as the ship descended into the depths of Geonosis. Once at the bottom, Saw and his rebel comrades discovered several poison canisters which provided compelling evidence that the Empire had perpetrated genocide against the Geonosians. Regretting his past behavior towards Klik-Klak, Saw argued that the Geonosians deserved the same right to rebuild as other peoples and released Klik-Klak and the Geonosian egg.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

After releasing Klik-Klak and taking several of the poison canisters, the ''Ghost'' managed to escape Geonosis by blasting through the Imperial light cruiser with [[proton torpedo]]es. Despite their successful escape, the rebels lost the poison canisters and were forced to make do with images of the canisters instead. Though Senator Organa and Commander [[Jun Sato]] regarded the mission as a success for rescuing Saw and obtaining a new [[deflector core]], Saw was disappointed that they still had not found out what the Empire was building on Geonosis. Kanan reassured him that they would eventually find out sooner or later.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

====Jalindi and a personal quest====
{{Quote|If you continue to allow this war to be fought on the Empire's terms, not yours, you are going to lose."<br />"I will not be lectured on military strategy by a man who has proven himself a criminal."<br />"The Empire considers ''both'' of us criminals. At least I ''act'' like one.|Saw Gerrera and Mon Mothma|<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion">{{Rebels|In the Name of the Rebellion}}</ref>}}
[[File:In_the_Name_-_Saw_Speaks.png|thumb|right|250px|Saw Gerrera clashed with Mon Mothma's Rebel Alliance over tactics.]]
In [[1 BBY]], Saw was first mentioned by Bail Organa, where he gave information that was supplied by Saw; primarily, a new [[Jalindi Station|relay]] being used by the Empire. When the Rebellion wanted to tap into the relay to learn what the Empire was doing, Saw, who had sent an [[R4-C2|astromech]], appeared and stated that they were cowards, as they were not doing what it would take to win. After [[Mon Mothma]] cut off communications with him, Saw prepared to head to the relay to destroy it. He arrived on his [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-Wing]] with the help of his pilot, [[Edrio]]. Upon opening the doors to drop bombs, he was surprised to see Ezra and Sabine, greeting the two while tossing out three packs of proton bombs onto the relay. Telling them that the bombs would detonate soon, he let them board his starfighter and proceeded to fly out of the area just as the bombs exploded, destroying the relay and killing [[Brom Titus]].<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />

Outside in Jalindi's space, Hera contacted him and told him to return Ezra and Sabine. Saw agreed and prepared the process; however, a [[Star Destroyer]] suddenly appeared, forcing Saw to leave for [[Faos Station]] with them. During the trip, Saw told the two that he needed their help as, after the events on Geonosis, he still did not know what the Empire was building. Upon arriving at Faos Station, he, Ezra, Sabine, and Chopper boarded [[Freighter 2716]].<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />

Upon investigating the materials, which were used for the construction of Star Destroyers, Saw claimed that the Empire was up to something. Continuing his investigation, they found Imperial stormtroopers on the ship and learned that the freighter was heading towards the remote [[Tonnis sector]], cementing Saw's suspicions. When Chopper told him that hold 12 contained an Imperial shuttle, they went in and found prisoners, who were either power or reactor technicians. Later on when Ezra kept hearing "singing," Chopper revealed that hold 17 was a restricted area. Upon opening the door to that hold, they encountered a [[death trooper]], prompting Saw to fire at point-blank range, killing the trooper. Sabine tossed several smoke grenades into the room, which Saw used to blend in and take down several troopers.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />

After clearing the area, [[DT-F16|one of the troopers]] managed to escape. Saw wanted to go after her, but Sabine told him not to. They inspected the mysterious cargo the troopers were protecting and realized that it was an unusually large [[kyber crystal]]. Saw, adamant in finding out what the Empire was building, reluctantly stayed to guard the [[crystal]] while Ezra and Sabine went to sabotage the hyperspace drive. However, he quickly betrayed them and stunned the two in the engine room.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />

When Ezra and Sabine woke up, they asked Saw why he betrayed them. Saw stated that they were very close to finding out the secret weapon and told them to look on the screen. When the freighter arrived at the Tonnis sector, they only saw a single Star Destroyer. Confused, but still convinced of the Empire's nefarious designs with the crystal, he used Ezra's lightsaber to destroy the freighter's hyperdrive before firing onto the crystal's mounting, effectively turning the crystal into a time bomb. He then freed the two, while Edrio, who had tailed the freighter, informed Saw that he was outside. Knowing that Ezra and Sabine no longer agreed with his methods, Saw bid farewell to them while they made their individual escapes before the freighter and Star Destroyer were obliterated.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />

====Mission to Dooma 4====
{{Quote|Hold On! We'll wait here for a while!|Saw Gerrera|<ref name="Crossing the Line">{{RebelsAnimationCite|4|Crossing the Line}}</ref>}}
Gerrera later learned that the [[Imperial Metal Factory]] on [[Dooma 4]] was providing components for a secret Imperial project. He and the Partisans undertook a [[Assault on Dooma 4|mission]] to the factory to blow up the station.<ref name="Crossing the Line" />

====Taking the fight to Jedha====
{{Quote|We are not insurgents. We are partisans. We are a rebellion. I bring battle-hardened fighters. I bring experienced tacticians. I bring pilots, a squadron of them. I bring the means with which to fight back. I am inviting you, both of you, to join me in this.|Saw Gerrera to Baze Malbus and Chirrut Îmwe|<ref name="Guardians of the Whills" />}}
[[File:Saw_Recruits_Chirrut_and_Baze.png|thumb|left|250px|Saw Gerrera meeting with Chirrut Îmwe and Baze Malbus and attempting to recruit them into his Partisans.]]
With his campaigns against the Empire becoming increasingly brutal, Alliance High Command, at the urging of Mon Mothma, [[Resolution of Censure Condemning Saw Gerrera of the Partisans|formally censured Gerrera]] and severed all official ties with the Partisans. By this time, Gerrera had lost his right leg and struggled to walk on a low-grade [[Cybernetics|cybernetic replacement]].<ref name="Rogue One" /> Additionally, beyond his years spent huffing rhydonium fumes,<ref name="TonyGilroy" /> his exposure to [[Insecticide|Geonosian insecticides]]<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> had scarred his [[lung]]s, confining him to a [[Saw Gerrera's suit|pressurized armor suit]].<ref name="Rogue One" /> Within that suit, however, he continued to suck down rhydonium fumes<ref name="TonyGilroy" /> through an oxygen mask.<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" />

Having previously learned that the Empire's massive kyber crystal had come from [[Jedha]], Gerrera relocated his militia to the moon, feeling that it was an appropriate place to bring his rebellion, as it was a sacred world to many different galactic religions.<ref name="Guardians of the Whills" /><ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> Due to the Imperials defiling many religious temples and artifacts in their pursuit of kyber crystals, small, local insurgent cells had begun forming in the Holy City of NiJedha in opposition to the occupation. From his new base of operations in the [[Catacombs of Cadera]], just a half-day's walk outside the Holy City, Gerrera began recruiting and organizing the local insurgencies under the umbrella of his Partisans.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /><ref name="Rogue One" /> During this time, he still held command over a pair of UT-60D U-wing troop transports and six T-65 X-wing fighters.<ref name="Rogue One" /><ref name="Saw Gerrera card">{{FFGXW|set=Saw's Renegades Expansion Pack|cardname=Saw Gerrera|ship=U-wing}}</ref>

Among the local insurgents Gerrera recruited were [[Guardians of the Whills]] [[Chirrut Îmwe]] and [[Baze Malbus]], whom he enticed into joining by providing much needed provisions for the [[Gimm sisters' orphanage|orphanage]] run by Îmwe and Malbus's friends, [[Kaya Gimm|Kaya]] and [[Killi Gimm]]. Over several months, the Partisans attacked the Imperial occupiers, leading to harsher and harsher reprisals from the Empire. The Star Destroyer that had previously orbited high over Jedha descended to rest right above the Holy City, and the number of [[stormtrooper]]s, tanks, and walkers on patrol in the streets increased significantly. Îmwe and Malbus came to Gerrera asking for assistance stealing a spacecraft so the Gimm sisters could flee the planet with their orphans. A group of Partisans, led by [[Beezer Fortuna]], helped Îmwe and Malbus steal a [[Sentinel-class landing craft|''Sentinel''-class shuttle]]. Under the orders of Gerrera, Fortuna and the other Partisans attempted to double-cross Îmwe and Malbus, wishing to use the shuttle to blow up the Star Destroyer over the city. Îmwe and Malbus were able to talk the Partisans out of taking the shuttle, allowing the orphans to escape Jedha. However, this led to Gerrera parting ways with Îmwe and Malbus.<ref name="Guardians of the Whills" />

====Reuniting with Jyn and death====
{{Quote|Save the Rebellion! Save the dream!|Saw Gerrera, to Jyn Erso, as Jedha is ripped apart|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
[[File:Saw_Gerrera_with_cane.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Gerrera meeting with Jyn Erso.]]
In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> just prior to the [[Battle of Scarif]], the Partisans captured [[Bodhi Rook]], a recently defected Imperial pilot. Bodhi carried a message from Galen Erso, who was trying to alert the Rebellion to the nearly-completed Death Star project. However, increasingly paranoid and believing that Imperial spies were everywhere, Gerrera was convinced that the defection was a trick by the Empire. To ascertain the truth, Gerrera used a [[mairan]] named [[Bor Gullet]] to read Rook's mind, at the risk of driving him insane. Afterward, he left the catatonic Rook in a cell, before deploying his men under Benthic and Edrio to attack an Imperial kyber convoy in [[Jedha City]]. In the ensuing firefight, [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service|Rebel intelligence]] Captain [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]], along with Jyn Erso, were captured: both were on the moon in search of Rook, whom the Rebel Alliance had learned had a message from Galen Erso.<ref name="Rogue One" />

Jyn and Cassian, along with Îmwe and Malbus, who had been caught up in the fighting, were brought to Saw's headquarters in the Catacombs of Cadera. Saw would see only Jyn. He questioned her on why she was there, demanding to know if she was there to kill him. She told him that she was there to ask for the message from her father and when it was given to the Rebel Alliance she would be on her way. Saw asked her why she did not believe in the dream of freedom throughout the galaxy. She told him about how he abandoned her at the age of sixteen and that his war did not mean anything to her. He then showed her the message from her father which revealed the weakness in the Empire's superweapon. However, as they spoke, [[Grand Moff]] Wilhuff Tarkin and Orson Krennic had resolved to test-fire the Death Star's [[superlaser]] on Jedha, having traced Bodhi there and seeing an opportunity to wipe out Saw's insurgency. A low-power shot [[Destruction of Jedha City|wiped out]] Jedha City in an instant and created a blast wave that spread for kilometers in every direction, threatening the Catacombs. Realizing the threat, Saw released his prisoners, commending Galen's message to Jyn and begging her to save the Rebellion. However, he declared that he would "run no longer" and remained in the Catacombs. After seeing Jyn's party escape, his last act was to tear off his breath mask before the blast wave consumed the Catacombs, killing him.<ref name="Rogue One" /> His last thoughts were for his late sister, Steela, and his last word was her name.<ref name="RO 3">[[Rogue One Adaptation 3|''Rogue One Adaptation'' 3]]</ref>

== Personality and traits ==

===General information===
Saw Gerrera was a human (Onderonian) male who was 1.80 [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Meter meters] tall with Gerrera also had dark skin. During the Clone War, his [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Hair hair] was [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Color black], with an orange [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Hair_dye stripe]. His hair later began graying and he stopped dying the orange stripe. Gerrera's [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Eye eyes] were blue, later becoming green before turning brown by the time of the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jedha_insurgency Jedha insurgency]. Gerrera had multiple cybernetics; a [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Cybernetics cybernetic] right [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Limb leg] as well as an [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Oxygen oxygen] [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Breath_mask respirator], a [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Saw_Gerrera's_suit pressurized suit of armor] and [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Armor reinforced] [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Lung lungs].   Gerrera had a addiction to the smell of and burning sensation of [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Rhydonium rhydonium] that dated back to his younger years;<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?2">{{Andor|Ever Been to Ghorman?}}</ref> During the Imperial era, it impacted his facilities as he believed he "understood" it and used no protection against its fumes.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?2" />

===Onderonian hero===
 {{Quote|I'm not a terrorist. I'm a patriot. And resistance is not terrorism.|Saw Gerrera|<ref name="The Soft War" />}} 

In his younger years, Saw Gerrera was a hot headed soldier who was eager for leadership and considered himself a patriot of [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Onderon Onderon]. A compassionate and charismatic man, Saw valued freedom, independence, and was a loyal follower of King [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Ramsis_Dendup Ramsis Dendup] willing to fight for causes supporting them.<ref name="The Soft War2">{{TCW|The Soft War}}</ref> While considered a terrorist in the eyes of Dendup's usurped administration and [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Confederacy_of_Independent_Systems Confederacy of Independent Systems], Gerrera considered himself a patriot, believed that resistance was not the same as terrorism.<ref name="The Soft War4">{{TCW|The Soft War}}</ref>  Having a competitive spirit and charm, he was also more aggressive than his fellow rebels and butted heads with his sister and Lux Bonteri alike; while she and many others wished to unite others with the support of the people, Saw instead desired to hurt his enemies and lacking this understanding became a flaw that once his sister a more popular leader, leaving him temporarily disheartened.<ref name="Front Runners"></ref><ref name="Dawn VG">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> The untimely death of his sister weighed heavily on his mind, sowing the seeds for him vowing to fight evil in all forms.<ref name="Ultimate, New">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref> 

[[File:SawGerrera19BBY.png|right|thumb|300x300px|In the early years of the Empire, Gerrera was a ruthless but charismatic hero of Onderon.]] In the early years of the Empire and it's transformation from the Republic, Gerrera's reputation was heightened for a time, marking him as a Onderonian hero and a candidate for the position of Governor of Onderon before he publicly rejected the Empire.<ref name="MOF22">''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''</ref> Retroactively considering himself more smart and prepared than he was during the Clone Wars at that point in his life,<ref name="Rebel Rising"></ref> Mothma noted upon meeting him for the first time, he moved with confidence akin to a chancellor or a judge and noted when accused of having no strategy by Organa, he revealed himself to be pragmatic, clever, more concerned for public opinion than he let on, having grand plans, ambitions, and capable of working with criminal elements to achieve his goals although she believed him limited to a single-[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sector sector] conflict. Fitting this image, he practiced giving speeches to inspire others to his cause. [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Haki_Zeophrine Haki Zeophrine] opined that Gerrera believed himself persecuted and any notion contradicting it frustrated him.<ref name="MOF">''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''</ref> 

Despite his public support of the Galactic Republic, he was skeptical about accepting their aid, believing it could lead to the Republic laying claim to Onderon should they emerge victorious in the war, a notion revealed to be true when it transformed into the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Dawn VG" /> Not believing him idealistic, he also believed people did not fight for principles or democracy despite their claims, instead yearning for resources, land, and self-preservation.<ref name="MOF" /> He also would strategize bold tactics, believing sacrifices to be worthwhile to achieve his goals.<ref name="The Summit"></ref> Through a combinations of his own actions as well as both accounts of the Empire and from allies alike,<ref name="Replacements22">{{TBB|Replacements}}</ref> be it true or falsified by both (the latter in other to give plausible deniability),<ref name="MOF22" /> Gerrera's image eroded overtime and leaned more into extremism.<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank"></ref>  

===An impassioned rebel===
 {{Quote|You target civilians, kill those who surrender, break every rule of engagement! If we degrade ourselves to the Empire's level, what will we become?''"<br />"''There she is! That's the leader the Rebellion needs! Where is that fire, that passion, when your people need it most? I hope, Senator, after you've lost, and the Empire reigns over the galaxy unopposed, you will find some comfort in the knowledge that you fought according to the rules.|Mon Mothma and Saw Gerrera|<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />}} [[File:Saw_Gerrera_SaV.png|left|thumb|270x270px|Although Gerrera fought for freedom against oppressors such as the Galactic Empire, his methods negatively affected his image.]] Long considered a extremist during the later years of the Imperial Era, he was unapologetic in his use of torture and could, at times, justify a slaughter on civilian targets such as the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mission_to_Inusagi mission to Inusagi].<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Retroactively, Gerrera disagreed with some of the Jedi's principled tactics, believing them lacking and costing them the Clone Wars.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis"></ref> He also pragmatically regarded their actions as being underwhelming despite their belief in the Force and powers associated with it.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Within his Partisan ranks, betrayal was considered a high cost, with summary execution from himself often being the punishment<ref name="Dawn VG" /> and held little regards for purging his own men for espionage against him, be it on behalf the Empire or Alliance.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /><ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> Alternatively, he would state his survival from spies and infiltrators from enemies (and supposed allies) was due to learning how to manipulate them to his wishes.<ref name="Jedha, Kyber, Erso">{{Andor|Jedha, Kyber, Erso}}</ref> He often found it frustrating that members of the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Alliance_to_Restore_the_Republic rebellion] worried about how they would be labelled being the Empire would classify them negatively regardless.<ref name="Rebel Rising" />    

Gerrera harbored great antipathy towards the Separatists for invading his homeworld Onderon.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix"></ref> He also disliked the Geonosians due to their alignment with the Separatists and for building gunships which led to his sister Steela's death. This coupled by the loss of his comrades during a mission on Geonosis led him to interrogate the Geonosian Klik-Klak, much to the discomfort of his former comrade Rex and the Spectres.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> Gerrera also develop paranoia as he became more battled-damaged and unstable, eventually believing both the Empire and Rebellion are conspiring to target him for his crimes.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /><ref name="Jedha, Kyber, Erso" /><ref name="The Soft War Episode Guide"></ref>  

While often upholding a callous exterior in most instances, Gerrera still retained a level of care and compassion he had in the earlier years of his lifetime;<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> Despite his antipathy towards the Geonosians, Gerrera was horrified by the Empire's genocide against the species and believed that they had the same right to rebuild as other species. leading him to concede with Erzra and release both Klik-Klak and the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Karina Geonosian queen egg] he was guarding.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> Despite partaking in the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mission_to_Inusagi mission to Inusagi] willingly and justifying it, he harbored a level of regret for it.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Often times, reluctant allies and friends alike commended Gerrera for his efforts in overtly combating the Empire when many in the galaxy were willing to overlook their atrocities.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion"></ref><ref name="Jedi: Survivor">''[[Star Wars Jedi: Survivor]]''</ref> He also held a conscience enough to show a level of reluctance in the idea of sacrificing those fighting against the Empire for a greater good even if he could accept and justify it.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix" />  

===Relationships===
====Allies, friends, and family====
=====Steela Gerrera=====
Saw loved cared for his younger sister profoundly, coming to see her potential as the best leader of the Onderon rebels even when he was at first dismayed at the fact.<ref name="Tipping Points"></ref> As siblings, the pair would often jokingly taunt one another. Her death would carry a powerful presence in his life, making him somewhat disillusioned with the Jedi in later years, believing their powers in the Force was limited from experiencing his sister's death.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Ultimately, he felt responsible for the death of his sister, Steela. Thus, he vowed to keep up his war against what he saw as evil, no matter what form his enemies took.  

=====Jyn Erso=====
{{Quote|''Jyn! My daughter!''|Saw Gerrera|<ref name="R1Novel" />}} The pair first meet during his early years of the Empire when he helped smuggled them off of [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Coruscant Corusant] to escape Krennic, with Jyn taking an immediate liking to him and considering him a friend.<ref name="Catalyst"></ref> Years later, a older Gerrera would take in the child as his ward<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> following losing her parents to the Empire and would come to view her as his daughter.<ref name="R1Novel"></ref> He mentored and trained her in how to defend herself and insurgent tactics but was paternally protective of Jyn and sought to protect her from even his own ranks. At the age of sixteen, Jyn believed she was abandoned by Gerrera and learned years later, upon reuniting with him, that he did so to protected her against Partisans whom would leverage her life to draw out Galen Erso, believed to be a Imperial scientist willingly working for the Empire and expressed he thought of Jyn frequently and missed her profoundly.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Despite his estranged relationship with Jyn, Gerrera was still able to inspire her to find the weakness in the Empire's superweapon in order to save the rebellion.<ref name="Rogue One"></ref> As he saw her stare in sadness at the holoprojector that had displayed her birth father, Gerrera felt shame and ire for a moment, pondering if she had grown soft, before kicking the thought from his mind. In his final moments with her, he decided Erso was still his best soldier and only remaining family.<ref name="R1Novel" />  

=====Lux Bonteri=====
While initially the pair fought alongside one another to free their home planet, Onderon, Gerrera often argued with Bonteri and accused him of being more politician than a soldier and/or a fighter and was disapproving of the affections his sister gave him, whom mediated the pair often. Their relationship improved, forming a more positive perception of him as they worked together to free Onderon.<ref name="A War on Two Fronts"></ref>  

===== Partisans =====
Gerrera had a trusted bond with both [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Benthic Benthic] and [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Edrio Edrio], both whom served the Partisans.<ref name="Edrio Two Tubes">{{Databank|edrio-two-tubes|Edrio Two Tubes}}</ref><ref name="Benthic Two Tubes">{{Databank|benthic-two-tubes|Benthic Two Tubes}}</ref> Sharing no reservation for his methods, the duo are among Gerrera's most trusted operatives, sharing operational information with them both in part due to their pain tolerance making them resistant to interrogation. While Edrio leads his [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Cavern_Angels Cavern Angels], Benthic operates as his informal rebel lieutenant and second-in-command.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> Gerrera held great respect for [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Cal_Kestis Cal Kestis], having offered him a place in his rebel cell and left the invitation open when he rejected it, in which Kestis helped on multiple occasion.<ref name="Jedi: Survivor2">''[[Star Wars Jedi: Survivor]]''</ref>   

Saw also held great care with [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Megyn_Soone Megyn Soone] and [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Idryssa_Barruck Idyrssa Barruck], both women compared to Steela and having ascended through the ranks (the former his Lieutenant).<ref name="Crossing the Line"></ref><ref name="Rebel Rising" /> While Idyrssa would disagree with his tactics, opted to side with the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Alliance_to_Restore_the_Republic Rebel Alliance], and the pair argued over ethics and strategy in fighting the Empire as a unified front, they maintained a mutual understanding and care. This care was profound enough for Jyn to observe arguing with her frustrated him to an extent and for him to perform missions on behalf of the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Alliance_to_Restore_the_Republic alliance] because she asked.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> With Megyn, despite convincing others his philosophy of rebelling against the Empire ("the mission") coming first at the expense of his own Partisans' lives and himself, he is unwilling to enact it against her, with Captain Engels observing his care for her.<ref name="Crossing the Line" /> 
=====Others=====
Saw was a longtime friend of Galen and Lyn Erso.<ref name="TSWB">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> Gerrera also held had a amicable relationship with spymaster [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Luthen_Rael Luthen Rael] although the latter's willingness to sacrifice allies caused him concern.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix" /> Saw harbored great respect for the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jedi_Order Jedi Order],<ref name="The Soft War">{{TCW|The Soft War}}</ref> persisting into his later years even as he held their tactics and reverence in the Force in doubt.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /><ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />

====Other relationships====
=====Bail Organa=====
Gerrera had a complicated relationship with Organa, whom he first met during the latter's [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Investigation_into_the_framing_of_the_Jedi secret investigation into the Jedi coup conspiracy] and interrogated him until both realized neither supported the Empire. Their relation with one another was chilly, with Organa critical of his methods and claiming he "fumbled" in military tactics against the Separatist and Empire and questioned his ethics, both notions that annoyed Gerrera. Gerrera believed Organa, like Mothma, to be tools of Palpatine ineffective at stopping him in the Senate and placated blame for the Clone Wars and the formation of the Empire on the Galactic Senate. Despite their differences, the two came to a unofficial alliance and understanding.<ref name="MOF3">''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''</ref> In later years, the pair could work together<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> but their relations deteriorated to the point where Organa believed him crazy.<ref name=":1">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref> Gerrera's dislike of Organa stemmed from when Organa covered his investigation, his involvement, and truth of the ordeal that took place in the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Attack_on_Eyo-Dajuritz attack on Eyo-Dajuritz], and portrayed himself as a supporter of the Empire to curtail Imperial espionage by framing Gerrera as a aggressive Onderonian terrorist to push the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Imperial_Rebirth_Act Imperial Rebirth Act], with Gerrera genuinely willing to work with Organa. He also disliked how Organa previously treated "him as a threat" in their initial meeting when their loyalties became known.<ref name="MOF3" /> 

=====Mon Mothma=====
Mothma met Gerrera personally shortly after the formation of the Galactic Empire, having heard of him and seen images of him prior. Mothma initially found him clever, confident, charismatic, and pragmatic, surprised he was more concerned with public support than he would let on, and believed his strategies sector-wide conflicts but believed his strategies to be limiting. In turn, Gerrera saw her as a tool for Palpatine and ineffective in stopping him through the Senate. . Despite their differences, Gerrera and Mothma came to an understanding although they never openly contacted one other unless circumstances were dire.<ref name="MOF3" /> The pair would meet several times over the years, arguing over strategies for the rebel to take and the existence of a superweapon for hours in meetings. Their mutual relationship deteriorated over the years and he would come to regard her as weak and indecisive leader, though he did see fire in her, while Mothma regarded him as a war criminal and terrorist mired in cynicism.<ref name="Rebel Files3">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>  

=====Alliance to Restore the Republic=====
{{Quote|I'm fighting for you and everyone else not to lose what they've got. And I won't apologize for how I do it.''"<br />"''Then you're no better than the Empire.|Saw Gerrera and Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />}} [[File:SawBailArgue-RogueOne2.png|right|thumb|270x270px|Saw Gerrera had a tenuous relationship with the other rebel cells.]]When Gerrera was first affiliated with the cell that eventually grew to be the Rebel Alliance, he and his Partisans had a reputation as effective soldiers and despite their tactics, they were initially welcomed.<ref name="Rebel Files3" /> This changed overtime, with Gerrera's view of them complex; some leaders criticized him for his lack of understanding people valuing peace more than freedom<ref name="Rebe Dossier2">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> and others believed he made it difficult for others to side with their efforts<ref name="Leia"></ref> and made him too comparable to the Empire.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> In turn, Gerrera believed them frustrating for their focus on labels from the Empire, disliked how their leaders prioritized which missions to engage, others seeking him out for aid only for more controversial and less convenient missions,<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> found them cowardly for following the rules of engagement when the Empire does not,<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> and eventually believed they conspired to assassinate him for his past crimes and extremism.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> However, despite his disillusionment, he supported their overall efforts, choosing to share his intel and urging his former protege Jyn to join and to save them.<ref name="Rogue One" /> 

==Skills and abilities==
===At all costs, even himself===
{{Quote|I will do whatever is required to be the victor.|Saw Gerrera, to Ezra Bridger|<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />}}
[[File:Saw_Gerrera_SWDL.png|thumb|left|200px|While a popular leader, he also held a reputation for being a ruthless and effective Rebel commander.]]
During the Clone Wars, Gerrera was trained by the Jedi Order in the art of combat,<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> affording him abilities in reconnaissance, infiltration, leadership,<ref name="Join the Battle">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]''</ref> and knowledge in weaponry and military tactics.<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> By the Imperial era, he garnered a reputation as a effective soldier,<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> considered among the [[Galactic Empire's Most Wanted list|Galactic Empire's Most Wanted]] a feared insurgent who employed ghastly tactics<ref name="Rebel Files2">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> and was ruthless, often taking no survivors.<ref name=":1">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref>

His abilities diminished overtime due to his failing health from a variety of factors: rhydonium fumes addiction,<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" /> adverse effects from barely hospitable hideouts,<ref name="Dawn VG" /> and a assassination attempt from [[teccitin]].<ref name="Guardians of the Whills" /> Beyond his habit of inhaling rhydonium,<ref name="TonyGilroy" /> he also sustained lung damage from Geonosian insecticides inhaled at near-lethal levels following a mission in Geonosis.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> An injury to his legs forced him to use a prosthetic leg.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Jyn Erso was upset to see him reduced to a weakened state during their reunion on Jedha, mentally comparing him to the force of nature he had once appeared as.<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" />

===Military commander===
[[File:Saw-Gerrera-full-body-RORD.png|thumb|right|200px|Saw Gerrera toward the end of his life]]
A popular rebel leader,<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> both himself<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> and his rebel cell gained a reputation for their effectiveness in the battlefield despite their tactics.<ref name="Rebel Files" /> In his earlier years, he was once considered for a position of Governor for Onderon and noted for his ability to inspire others towards resistance, practicing speeches in order to help his agenda in recruitment. Mothma believed his agenda were suited for potential sector-wide success.<ref name="MOF" /> During his campaigns against the Empire, he had successful endeavors such as his victories in the [[Arkanis sector]], noted for being a rare display of anti-Empire ruthlessness from resistance movements and making things difficult for the Moff in charge of the sector.<ref name="Rebel Files2" />  

Gerrera was adept at assessing people and groups, a skill he taught to Jyn Erso after taking her in as his ward and protege.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Although paranoia impacted this later in his lifetime,<ref name="Rogue One" /> his assessments were often correct; his assessment of the Maya Pei Brigade was accurate,<ref name="Narkina 5" /> with the disappearance of their leader impacting them.<ref name="Sagrona Teema">{{Andor|Sagrona Teema}}</ref> He also predicted the existence of the Empire building a superweapon (the Death Star).<ref name="Rogue One" /><ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> When investigating kyber crystals and the superweapon, the Empire was prompted to move it's location elsewhere due to how close Gerrera came to uncovering it.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> Imperial Commander [[Kanchar]] noted Gerrera's efforts also captured a lot of kyber crystals from the Empire, admiring him for being competent his capabilities.<ref name="Star Wars 2015 39">[[Star Wars (2015) 39|''Star Wars'' (2015) 39]]</ref> He also uncovered spies within his ranks (both Imperial and Rebel alike)<ref name="Rebel Files" /><ref name="Rebel Rising" /><ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" /> and could using them for misdirection.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />  

Despite his capabilities, Mothma and other rebel leaders in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] believed his methods would often cause more problems for them, the former criticizing his actions often ostracized potential recruitment of powerful political candidates and believed him too pessimistic and underestimating of people's desire towards peace.<ref name="Rebel Files" /> [[Luthen Rael|Rael]] was also critical of his hesitance to near-inability to work alongside other rebel cells he didn't align with.<ref name="Narkina 5" /> His methods also collided with his own members at times, the [[Mission to Inusagi|Inusagi mission]] in particular causing others to move towards other rebel cells.<ref name="Rebel Rising" />

===Combat abilities===
In combat, Gerrera was skilled in both armed and unarmed combat.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> His unarmed skills were formidable enough to overpower Ezra Bridger, Rex,<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> and incapacitate both [[stormtrooper]]s and [[death trooper]]s.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> He could also use a variety of melee weaponry such as staves (in which he favored), truncheons, and knives in addition to ranged weaponry like a blaster, snipers, and explosives. He taught much of his combat skills to his protege, [[Jyn Erso]], who noted him to be rather quick and taught her to employ dirty tactics.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> 

===Other skills===
Like other [[Onderonian outcasts]], Gerrera could also domesticate other animals such as a [[ruping]].<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> He was a trained pilot and experience in the Clone Wars also made him knowledgeable in various droid models and their weaknesses.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Gerrera was also an expert at interrogation and intimidation, employing ghastly techniques and unethical means to acquire information,<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> allowing him to gain intelligence and information more accurate than his Alliance counterparts despite being less well-equipped.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> Conversely, he displayed resistance against interrogation and torture himself during the Clone Wars,<ref name="The Soft War Episode Guide" /> although this unintentionally hardened him into a remorseless warrior.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" />

==Equipment==
Gerrera wielded multiple weapons; including an [[A140 blaster pistol]], a [[sniper rifle]],<ref name="Front Runners" /> and a [[DC-15A blaster carbine]].<ref name="The Soft War" /> Gerrera wore several different suits that acted as armor; he bore a [[Saw Gerrera's suit|pressurized suit]] sometime prior to his mission on Kashyyyk consisting of a [[plastoid]] ailette blackblast armor and a atmospheric sensor sampler and a Onderon banner he wore as a cape.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /><ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" /> The suit would later also have a ventilator breaking tube.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /><ref name="Rogue One" /> He alternated with a lighter, green-colored [[Environment suit|vac-suit]] with a hermetic coupler, sealing wrist cuff, and corrugated articulation in the legs and arms.<ref name="Dawn VG" /> He often carried a [[DH-16 Blaster Pistol|DH-16 blaster pistol]] with a perforated cooling sleeve and also contained a grappling hook attachment within the weapon.<ref name="Dawn VG" /><ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Development===
{{Quote|Saw Gerrera is maybe the original rebel. He is the first one in a long line of people that got trained by Jedi to fight for themselves; to save their planets during the Clone Wars. He's the beginning of what would eventually become the Rebel Alliance.|Dave Filoni, on Saw Gerrera|<ref name="YouTube The Original Rebel">{{SWYouTube|mLN_y-uWAVA|The Original Rebel: Saw Gerrera Returns | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/disneyxd-saw-gerrera-returns-in-the-name-of-the-rebellion-preview-star-wars-rebels}}</ref>}}
The character of Saw Gerrera was voiced in the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''<ref name="Kishino interview">{{SW|url=news/interview-andrew-kishino-saw-gerrera-on-the-clone-wars|text=Interview: Andrew Kishino - Saw Gerrera on ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> and ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]'' by [[Andrew Kishino]].<ref name="TBBAftermath" /> Saw Gerrera was played by [[Forest Whitaker]] in the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="Rogue One" /> who returned to voice the character in ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> and the [[2019]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]''.<ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" /> He was originally conceived by ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] for the unproduced live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: Underworld]]''<ref name="New-R1">{{StarWarsShow|Filn82qphCA|New Rogue One Characters Revealed, LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures|sw_url=video/the-star-wars-show-episode-7}}</ref> and Lucas later wanted to involve the character in an arc in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] of ''The Clone Wars'',<ref name="Filoni interview">{{SW|url=news/interview-dave-filoni-on-star-wars-the-clone-wars-season-five-part-1|text=Interview: Dave Filoni on ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Season Five, Part 1}}</ref> where he first appeared in the episode "[[A War on Two Fronts]]",<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> which premiered on [[October 6]], [[2012]].<ref name="A War on Two Fronts EG old">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep502|text="A War on Two Fronts" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref> ''The Clone Wars'' and ''Rebels'' showrunner [[Dave Filoni]] described Gerrera as "the original rebel" because he was "the first one in a long line of people" who were trained by the Jedi during the Clone Wars as planetary defense insurgents. To Filoni, Gerrera is the beginning point for what eventually becomes the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="YouTube The Original Rebel" />

Accordingly, the character's name is a "mnemonic riff" on real-life [[Wikipedia:Argentinia|Argentinian]] revolutionary and associate of [[Wikipedia:Fidel Castro|Fidel Castro]] - [[Wikipedia:Che Guevara|Che Guevara]] as revealed in ''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. [[Lucasfilm Story Group]]'s [[Kiri Hart]] was the one who suggested that the character be used in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="The Art of Rogue One">''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> An inspiration for Gerrera's character in ''Rogue One'', according to [[Phil Szostak]], was [[Wikipedia:Colonel Kurtz|Colonel Kurtz]] from the novella ''[[Wikipedia:Heart of Darkness|Heart of Darkness]]'', adapted as [[Wikipedia:Francis Ford Coppola|Francis Ford Coppola's]] [[1979]] film [[Wikipedia:Apocalypse Now|''Apocalypse Now'']].<ref name="Talin In VII?">{{Twitter|PhilSzostak|status/943942175389138944|[[Phil Szostak]]|quote=Colonel Kurtz also served as inspiration for exiled rebel extremist Saw Gerrera in #RogueOne. The character is based on ivory trader Kurtz from Joseph Conrad's novella Heart of Darkness, one of my favorite books. #StarWars|archivedate=20191211171159}}</ref> [[Pablo Hidalgo]] of the Lucasfilm Story Group also stated that Gerrera's origin in the Clone Wars<ref name="PabloCommentary1">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3lotk4idfb22j|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2025-05-10|quote=Wait’ll people find out what the Onderon arc of TCW that debuted Saw Gerrera was inspired by. 👀|archivedate=20260303232534}}</ref> was inspired by the [[Wikipedia:Operation Cyclone|US government arming Mujahideen fighters in Afghanistan]] to battle the [[Wikipedia:USSR|USSR]], with Hidalgo specifically noting how Gerrera and his comrades were supplied with rocket launchers to take down enemy gunships.<ref name="PabloCommentary2">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3lotknmu7os2j|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2025-05-10|quote=The Republic covertly supplying rocket launchers to the freedom fighters to take out enemy gunships certainly seems familiar! {{C|In response to: "Wasn't there a direct parallel to the US government sending munitions to the Mujahideen?"}}|archivedate=20260303233029}}</ref> According to writer [[Gary Whitta]], Forest Whitaker was the only actor they considered to play Gerrera in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Only Forest">{{Twitter|garywhitta|status/1219451136572133377|[[Gary Whitta]]|quote=Yes. Forrest was always the only choice for Saw.|archivedate=20200121030231}} {{C|in response to "''Did you have any actors in mind when writing Rogue One? And did any of these wishes get realised? (Doubt you'd tell us any of the actors you wished for but it didn't pan out?)''"}}</ref>

Andrew Kishino had been a huge ''[[Star Wars]]'' fan growing up. Kishino had auditioned for the role as he thought that the character description had been a perfect fit of him. The script that had been sent out had been anomynized, with the character's names having been changed and the production name having been abreviated as "CW.", leading Kishino to think that it would be for a production of the television network [[Wikipedia:The CW|The CW]], and he only realized it when he turned up and saw Kenobi's voice actor [[James Arnold Taylor]]. The voice actors all recorded their lines together in a group.<ref name="Kishino interview" /> Kishino and Steela Gerrera's actor [[Dawn-Lyen Gardner]] had been friends already prior to working together on the series, but hadn't known that the other had been cast before meeting at the first session.<ref name="Steela interview">{{SW|url=news/interview-dawn-lyen-gardner-steela-gerrera-on-the-clone-wars|text=Interview: Dawn-Lyen Gardner — Steela Gerrera on ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> Gerrera was modeled after the likeness of Kishino, and he his face was recorded for two of the four episodes and as such the character also shared some of his facial mannerisms. Kishino compared Gerrera's personality in the arc to that of a leader who is hard to everyone, but still cared for them like a big brother; comparing him to an [[Wikipedia:Alpha wolf|alpha wolf]] and his expirience with the subcultures of [[Wikipedia:Hip-hop|hip-hop]] and [[Wikipedia:New York|New York]]. Kishino had been thrilled and grateful when Filoni said that his character could end up as an action figure, due to him only having few ''Star Wars'' toys growing up in poor circumstances and his attatchment to them.<ref name="Kishino interview" />

===''Andor'' return===
[[File:Andor_Saw_Gerrera_Poster.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Forest Whitaker as Saw Gerrera in his character poster]]
Whitaker reprised his role as Gerrera in the episodes "[[Narkina 5 (episode)|Narkina 5]]"<ref name="Narkina 5" /> and "[[Daughter of Ferrix]]" in the ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' television series.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix" /> Executive producer and writer [[Tony Gilroy]] wanted Gerrera and the other legacy characters to not provide fan service.<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How ‘Andor' Became the First ‘Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: ‘I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> The night before a rehearsal for Gerrera and Luthen Rael's argument in "Narkina 5," Whitaker asked director [[Toby Haynes]] questions about backstory and kyber crystals. During the rehearsal, Whitaker and Rael's actor, [[Stellan Skarsgård]], read the scene for the first time and went at each other. According to Haynes, when the scene was filmed for real, Whitaker and Skarsgård almost deconstructed what they did in a natural and spontaneous way. They then had to completely reconstruct the scene, and it was hard to get to the same pitch. Haynes wanted to end Gerrera's rant with a very direct, face-on shot of Whitaker to build the intensity and bring the audience into the argument. To accomplish this, Haynes had Whitaker do his speech several times, telling him to "go crazy with it."<ref name="Career Highlight">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-episode-8-toby-haynes-forest-whitaker-stellan-skarsgard-1235250954|text=‘Andor' Director Toby Haynes Talks That Forest Whitaker-Stellan Skarsgard Scene: “It Was a Career Highlight”|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-10-28|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221029050743}}</ref>

According to Gilroy, at the time of ''Rogue One'', the crew did not have an answer to what Gerrera was inhaling through his breathing mask. However, for Gerrera's return in [[Andor Season 2|''Andor'' Season 2]], writer [[Beau Willimon]] proposed to Gilroy that Gerrera was inhaling rhydonium fuel fumes, which Gilroy liked. According to Gilroy, Luthen Rael giving Gerrera the ability to steal fuel was a gift that firmed up their bond forever. Gerrera's speech about rhydonium<ref name="RhydoHigh">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/andor-creator-tony-gilroy-explains-saw-gerrera-mask-sucking-origin-story-11723317|text=Andor creator Tony Gilroy explains Saw Gerrera mask-sucking origin story|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2025-05-02|archivedate=20250503021646}}</ref> in the episode "[[I Have Friends Everywhere]]"<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" /> was written by Willimon, with Gilroy then doing a first pass on the speech and loving what was put down.<ref name="RhydoHigh" /> While the [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One'' novelization]] by [[Alexander Freed]]<ref name="R1Novel" /> and [[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel|junior novelization]] by [[Matt Forbeck]] had previously suggested Gerrera was inhaling oxygen by identifying Gerrera's breathing mask as an oxygen mask,<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" /> [[StarWars.com]] confirmed that Gerrera had been inhaling rhydonium through his<ref name="TonyGilroy" /> oxygen mask<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" /> during the events of ''Rogue One''.<ref name="TonyGilroy" />

===Concept art===
[[File:Bizarre_Saw_Gerrera_concept_art.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Early conceptual art for Saw Gerrera's live-action appearance in ''Rogue One'' by Aaron McBride inspired by Colnel Kurtz]]
Character illustration concept art of Gerrera for ''The Clone Wars'' was done by [[Tara Rueping]]<ref name="A War on Two Fronts EG" /> and a character illustration of him with a cloak for the "[[The Soft War]]" was done by [[Will Nichols]] and [[Carlos Sanchez]].<ref name="The Soft War Episode Guide" /> and finished on [[January 19]], [[2011]].<ref name="10 things">{{SW|url=news/10-things-you-should-know-about-saw-gerrera-from-the-clone-wars|text=10 Things You Should Know About Saw Gerrera from ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> For ''Rogue One'' concept art of the character was done by multiple artists: [[Aaron McBride]] designed a piece with Gerrera on a "throne" in a jungle with a pile of Imperial helmets on the ground<ref name="The Art of Rogue One" /> in [[2014]]. The piece, inspired by Colnel Kurtz,<ref name="ArtStation McBride">{{ArtStation|username=aaronmcbride|url=artwork/1rwx8|name=Aaron McBride|text=Saw Gerrera sitting on Throne Concept . Rogue One: A Star Wars Story ( 2016 )|quote=Ha. Yeah this was back in 2014. I tried making him a little more "Col. Kurtz" back then.|archivedate=20200603182812}}</ref> depicted him white skin and robotic right arm and legs and had a scarred face missing his left eye. [[Adam Brockbank]] also produced a piece with him in a yellow suit with breathing tubes, while Brockbank and [[Glyn Dillon]] designed multiple pieces of his final design. Other pieces featuring him were also done by [[Thom Tenery]], [[Erik Tiemens]], [[Will Htay]]<ref name="The Art of Rogue One" /> and [[Vincent Jenkins]].<ref name="Vincent Jenkins">{{Twitter|vincentj_artist|status/1985360297968975972|[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2025-11-03|quote="Rogue One" early idea for Saw Gerrera. #StarWars|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/Yqwux|archivefile=File:VincentJenkins-EarlyRogueOneSaw-Twitter.png}}</ref> Concept art of Gerrera's costume for ''Andor'' was done by costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]]<ref name="AndorCostumeConcept">{{Instagram|username=michaelwilkinson|url=p/DNTRW-BRRp6|name=[[Michael Wilkinson]]|date=2025-08-14|quote=I wanted to share more details of mighty #SawGerrara , played by the wonderful @forestwhitaker - in #Andor, we portrayed Saw 5 years before #RogueOne - a bit younger, and not yet completely weighed down by his addictions and obsessions. Shown in this post too are some of his militia - a motley crew of humans and creatures! #costumes #costumedesign #starwars #fyc|archiveurl=https://archive.is/1HVOZ}}</ref> Gerrera's model for ''The Bad Batch'' was finished by [[Jason Pichon]] on [[April 19]], 2019.<ref name="Aftermath EG">{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/aftermath-episode-guide|text="Aftermath" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}}</ref>
